## 固定收益開篇主論

美國公債8月21日收低。意外強勁的企業活動使賣壓轉向對政策較敏感的年期，也扭轉本週因財政疑慮造成的部分殖利率曲線陡峭化。2年期殖利率上升4.7個基點至4.237%，5年期上升3.4個基點至4.425%，10年期上升2.9個基點至4.735%，30年期則上升2.3個基點至5.272%。

這波跌勢幅度不大，但結構更值得注意。標普全球指標顯示，美國企業活動以逾四年來最快速度擴張，即使就業、零售銷售及基礎通膨數據轉弱，聯準會仍可能需要升息。10年期實質殖利率上升4.8個基點至2.402%，10年期損益兩平通膨率反而下降1.9個基點至2.333%。因此，週五名目殖利率上升的主因是實質利率，而非延續前一日由能源帶動的通膨重新定價。

短端表現落後，2年期與10年期利差收窄1.8個基點至49.8個基點，2年期與30年期利差也收窄2.4個基點至103.5個基點。前一交易日，通膨補償與長端財政壓力曾使曲線小幅陡峭化，週五走勢則有所轉變。不過，這並未逆轉幅度大得多的單月行情：30年期殖利率一個月來仍上升13.9個基點，2年期同期則下降2.7個基點，長期財政與存續期間溢價依然存在。

財政部長Scott Bessent擴大公債回購的計畫已不再帶動殖利率下降。財政部週中承諾，至少加倍買進部分10年至30年期公債，當時引發一波強勁但短暫的漲勢；到了週末，10年期與30年期殖利率分別收在4.735%及5.272%。交易員仍在等待Bessent承諾提出的財政方案細節，同時評估殖利率若再度上升，財政部是否會調整長期公債發行。總統Donald Trump週五表示，Bessent是依自身職權決定干預，並非奉總統指示行事。

跨資產市場一方面反映債市疲弱，另一方面也顯示風險偏好仍具韌性，投資人持續尋求美元資產以外的選擇。標普500指數上漲0.43%，那斯達克100指數上漲0.33%；費城半導體指數則下跌0.51%，全週跌幅達5.45%。美元指數週五下跌0.10%，全週下跌0.87%。黃金期貨上漲2.39%至$4,624.10，全週漲幅擴大至5.56%。比特幣則在空頭回補與資金重新流入帶動下，創逾三年來最大單週漲幅，交易價格約為$77,000。

原油並未向利率市場發出一致的通膨訊號。WTI下跌0.88%至$87.06，布蘭特原油卻上漲0.65%至$94.39，全週漲幅達6.63%。伊朗總統Masoud Pezeshkian呼籲結束戰爭，一度使油價自盤中高點回落；但其他伊朗官員仍主張繼續作戰，油價隨後回升。10年期損益兩平通膨率下降，顯示週五美債賣壓不只是原油行情的再次反映；景氣活動轉強與實質殖利率上升才是更清楚的解釋。

信用融資管道仍然暢通，但資金配置日益反映AI投資週期的成本與規模。殖利率高於7%的投資級資料中心專案吸引高收益債投資人參與；Alphabet創紀錄的澳幣債交易，則同時顯示替代融資市場的廣度與承接上限。在困境債方面，中國大陸法院下令沒收創辦人許家印的資產，使恆大境外債權人的回收程序更加複雜；Braskem的債權人保護期限將屆，重整條件卻仍未達成協議。

## 強勁景氣活動考驗財政部干預的極限

週五美債走勢顯示，市場對回購行情持久性的信心迅速消退。兩天前，擴大回購長天期公債的消息帶來官方買盤，推動既有10年至30年期公債殖利率大幅下降。但到了週末，經濟成長、通膨、赤字及企業發債競爭再度主導市場出清水準，殖利率溢價已回升大半。

標普全球活動指標轉強，使聯準會政策重新納入定價考量。2年期殖利率上升4.7個基點，漲幅高於所有較長年期指標；由於損益兩平通膨率下降，實質殖利率的升幅也超過10年期名目殖利率。這並非新一輪通膨恐慌。市場的判斷是，即使近期就業與零售數據較弱，強勁的企業動能仍可能讓決策者更難忽視高於目標的通膨。

週五利率交換市場顯示，9月升息機率約40%，到年底前後才完整反映一次升息。7月聯邦公開市場委員會會議有3名委員投下支持升息的異議票，此後也有數名無投票權官員表態支持緊縮，因此相關預期仍取決於後續通膨數據。另一方面，溫和的基礎通膨，以及偏弱的就業與支出數據，使市場尚未形成確定的緊縮共識。

回購計畫作用於殖利率曲線的另一端。Bessent將財政部的做法稱為「公債扭轉操作」：買進較長天期債券，同時提高短債在融資中的比重。這類期限轉換可以減少民間投資人必須承接的存續期間風險，卻不會降低借款總額，並使政府融資成本對未來短期利率更加敏感。聯邦債務已超過$40兆，每年利息支出也高於$1兆，投資人仍在等待證據，確認債務管理措施會與縮小赤字並行。

Bessent表示，他將與白宮預算局局長Russ Vought一併檢視收入與支出，包括減少詐欺和降低對各州的移轉支出。截至週五收盤，政府尚未提出量化的財政效果。社會安全、Medicare與Medicaid是赤字預估接近GDP 6%的主要原因；Evercore ISI策略師Sarah Bianchi認為，若不調整受到政治保護的計畫，短期內不太可能取得實質節省。

財政部也可能改變未來標售的期限組合。近期發債指引調整後，市場開始猜測，官員可能限制最長天期公債的發售，將新增借款集中於國庫券及中期公債。Bessent另行呼籲AI企業考慮多發行5年期債券，避免繼續增加長端供給。這些措施可以改變供給流向投資人的位置，但政府與企業部門仍須競逐同一個整體資金池。

相關不確定性也使債務管理的可預測性受到質疑。財政部表示，回購旨在改善既有公債的流動性，但摩根大通利率策略師發現，今年市場運作已有顯著改善。因此，投資人可能把進一步干預解讀為財政部針對殖利率水準採取行動，而非例行的流動性操作。Western Asset投資組合經理Robert Abad表示，若再度增加買進或調整長端發行，將更能證明官員是在回應借款成本本身。

週五交易量低於前一日。FINRA記錄的美國公債面額交易量為$9,797億，下降21.4%；其中名目附息債交易量為$8,324億，下降18.1%。20年以上年期的交易量下降35.8%至$885億。這些數字無法顯示客戶是買進或賣出，但說明殖利率上升之際，成交量正自最初干預後較劇烈的調整水準回落。

壓力也由美債市場轉向其他資產。黃金上漲、美元走弱與比特幣飆升，反映市場擔心壓低長期殖利率的措施，可能把部分調整壓力轉移至匯率或稀缺資產。比特幣週五一度上漲9.4%；三天內約有$25億的比特幣空頭部位遭清算，加密貨幣整體清算金額則達$45億。美國上市的比特幣現貨基金全週吸引逾$10億流入。

空頭被迫回補占加密貨幣漲勢很大一部分，因此限制了比特幣作為純粹財政訊號的解讀價值。黃金並無相同的清算機制，月初至今仍上漲約13.58%。美元指數降至98.8，一個月來下跌2.35%。財政部干預未能帶來持久的債市漲勢，最常被視為貨幣與財政避險的資產卻守住漲幅。

股票市場的反應較不偏向防禦。強勁活動數據支持獲利展望，標普500與那斯達克100指數上漲，VIX則下跌5.50%至15.13。不過，標普500全週仍下跌1.43%，那斯達克100下跌2.45%，半導體股的週跌幅更大。即使大盤指數上漲，實質殖利率走高與AI建設的融資負擔，仍持續抬高高久期股票的估值門檻。

市場訊號因觀察期間而異。週五景氣活動強勁，推升近期實質利率預期並使殖利率曲線趨平；若拉長至一個月，龐大的政府借款、持續的通膨不確定性與民間資金需求，仍使長端承受更大壓力。擴大回購可以暫時改變壓力分布，但週五收盤顯示，這項措施並未取代決定殖利率的經濟與財政力量。

## AI融資吸引高收益債投資人跨足投資級債

AI資本支出週期正日益模糊投資級與高收益債需求的傳統界線。QTS Realty Trust發行$39億債券，為喬治亞州一項與Microsoft有關的資料中心專案融資，殖利率約7.23%。這批債券具投資級評等，但殖利率高於許多中等評級非投資級借款人通常支付的水準，因此承銷商同時配售給投資級與高收益債投資人。

BlackRock在7月為德州資料中心專案融資時，投資級債券殖利率甚至高達7.53%。次級市場上，包括Oracle與SpaceX在內的發行人債務，也以通常與垃圾債相當的殖利率成交。這類跨界需求顯示，投資人正區分正式信用評等與實際所需補償；後者涵蓋施工風險、租戶集中、反覆發債及專案回報不確定性。

2026年至今，企業為資料中心及其他AI投資借款已超過$4,100億。Vanguard估計，超大規模雲端業者今年支出可能接近$8,000億，2027年至2030年每年則超過$1兆，而且大部分支出將由債券市場融資。這批預期供給說明，即使是評等很高的專案，也必須提供足以吸引傳統投資級買方以外投資人的殖利率。

新增買盤雖有助益，承接能力卻有限。美國高收益債市場規模約$1.5兆，不到投資級市場的五分之一；若要大幅轉進高評等科技債，高收益債投資人必須出售既有部位籌措資金。因此，跨界買盤可以擴大個別交易的配售範圍，卻無法為整體融資管線提供無限容量。

較高殖利率最終可能自行抑制發行量。資產負債表穩健的大型科技公司能夠承受昂貴的融資成本，等待多年後資料中心投資產生現金流；規模較小的借款人則沒有同等空間。摩根士丹利策略師預期，利差擴大將率先限制較低評等發行人。即使最大型的超大規模業者持續支出，融資成本仍可能成為未來供給的煞車。

Alphabet的澳幣債交易則從另一角度考驗市場容量。公司首次在澳洲發債便籌得A$55億，創下當地企業債發行紀錄，訂單金額超過A$180億。這筆交易是Alphabet今年發債逾$800億的一部分，所用幣別涵蓋美元、加幣、澳幣、歐元、瑞士法郎、英鎊與日圓。

澳洲市場提供幣別多元化及深厚的退休基金買盤，Alphabet也可利用交叉貨幣交換，把所得資金轉換為所需幣別。其20年期澳幣債換回美元後，定價大致與美國市場的借款成本相當。對當地投資人而言，這筆交易提供大型國際發行人，其殖利率高於評等相近的澳洲本地銀行債。

配售結果也揭示市場上限。Queensland Investment Corporation在各券次合計申購A$3億，最終獲配約A$1.7億。該公司固定收益策略主管Marayka Ward預期，大型科技公司將發行更多債券，但她認為澳洲每年可能只能容納幾筆這種規模的交易。她也表示，另一家超大規模業者未必會像Alphabet一樣受到市場歡迎，尤其是當投資人認為其業務防禦性較弱時。

外國借款人今年已發行逾A$640億澳幣債，市場可望再創年度紀錄。然而，相較於美國約$1.5兆的投資級發行量，這個總額仍然很小。澳洲可以為特定發行人提供融資多元化，但無法以美國市場的規模承接整體超大規模業者融資管線。

市場擴張也正在改變避險活動。近月3年期澳洲公債期貨未平倉量週四達140萬口，創2019年5月以來新高，並接近2008年創下的143萬口紀錄。澳幣債券市值自2022年10月低點以來增加近40%，達A$2.14兆，帶動交易商與投資人提高利率風險避險需求。

即使企業信用品質沒有惡化，這些發展仍把AI融資熱潮直接連結至主權債殖利率曲線。大型專案與企業發債增加存續期間供給、占用交易商資產負債表，並與政府競逐投資人。投資級評等可維持融資管道暢通，但殖利率超過7%的交易顯示，這類融資必須以反映建設規模與不確定性的成本才能成交。

## 通膨與成長分化，各國政策訊號背離

歐洲薪資與通膨預期數據轉佳，但尚不足以釐清歐洲央行是否需要再次升息。第2季協議薪資較一年前上升2.44%，低於前一季修正後的2.56%，也遠低於2024年的5.55%高點。薪資增幅放緩，削弱能源衝擊迅速傳導至工資的跡象；不過，歐洲央行追蹤指標預計，增幅到2027年初仍可能有所加快。

消費者通膨預期也小幅下降。歐洲央行7月調查顯示，家庭預期未來一年物價上升2.9%，低於6月的3%；3年期預期則由2.8%降至2.7%。雖然兩者仍高於歐洲央行2%的目標，但在伊朗衝突造成油氣市場大幅波動後，下降方向仍令人稍感安心。

歐洲央行管理委員會成員Martins Kazaks並未排除任何政策選項。他形容接近3%的通膨略令人不安，並表示央行已準備好在必要時採取行動，但強調9月決策將取決於更新後的數據與預測。他也提到第2季成長高於預期、失業率偏低，同時承認薪資正在放緩，通膨預期仍受到控制。

這項組合使歐洲央行必須在當前通膨與二輪效應仍受抑制的證據之間權衡。6月首次升息後，市場已接近反映再升息25個基點。薪資與預期數據使立即緊縮不再那麼順理成章，但能源成本若持續偏高，或擴散至服務價格與企業定價，風險仍未消除。

瑞士面臨的是通膨問題的另一端。瑞士央行決策官員Petra Tschudin表示，若有必要讓通膨維持在0%至2%的區間，央行將把利率降至零以下。瑞士央行去年把政策利率降至零後一直維持不變；儘管全球能源價格上升，7月通膨仍放緩至0.4%。第2季成長優於預期與薪資上升提供相反證據，但Tschudin的說法保留了負利率工具，並未把零視為利率下限。

南韓貿易數據則強化進一步緊縮的理由。8月前20天，按工作日調整後的出口較一年前上升61.5%；可比的7月期間最初公布增幅為62.9%。未經調整的出口增加56%，進口增加19%，貿易順差接近$140億。

半導體出口大增198.8%，居各類產品之首；電腦相關出口則增加242.1%。對中國出口上升118.6%，對美國出口上升59.4%；汽車出口卻下滑約45%，顯示成長動能仍集中在科技業，並未均勻分布於各產業。

韓國央行7月升息25個基點至2.75%，並維持緊縮傾向。此後整體通膨放緩至2.8%，核心通膨卻加速至2.6%，第2季經濟成長率也達到高於預期的0.6%。出口激增提高經濟承受再次升息的能力，使下次會議的選擇落在連續第二次升息，或等待至10月再行動。

日本面對的組合則是貨幣政策正常化與財政供給。預計明年4月開始的會計年度，預算申請總額將超過先前¥122兆的紀錄。日本財務省正考慮採用3.8%的暫定利率估算明年度債務服務成本，高於本會計年度計畫的2.6%。利息支出目前已占預算約四分之一，若採用較高假設，JGB殖利率上升便會直接反映在官方支出估算中。

不過，預算申請總額可能高估實際財政擴張。首相高市早苗希望把經常性計畫由補充預算移至初始預算，因此去年¥18.3兆追加預算中的部分支出，可能只是提早出現在編列程序。各部會也可透過另一套多年期架構，為與¥370兆、為期14年的成長策略相關資本投資申請不設上限的資金；這套架構部分將以過渡性債券融資。

這些變更使歷史比較更加困難，卻未消除融資負擔。各部會預計下週開始提出申請，最終預算及公債發行計畫則要到年底前後才會明朗。投資人必須區分：數字增加究竟只是更透明地揭露既有支出，還是代表真正擴大承諾；尤其在假設利率提高後，既有債務再融資與新增發行的成本都將上升。

中國週末公布的成長評估，則為全球景氣增添需求轉弱訊號。高盛估計，第3季初年化經濟增速已由前季的4.3%降至約4%，低於北京設定的全年4.5%至5%目標。法國巴黎銀行估計為4.1%，麥格理則估計約4.2%。7月工業生產、消費與投資疲弱，使高盛將這波放緩定性為需求驅動。

貨幣寬鬆預期因而升高，但油價與工業品出廠價格上漲限制了政策空間。7月受訪經濟學家普遍預期，中國人民銀行今明兩年都會維持政策利率不變，但認為第4季調降銀行存款準備率的可能性較高。迄今官員偏好貸款補貼與其他定向融資支持，尚未採取廣泛降息。

全球政策分化仍有利於部分新興市場利差交易。由8種主要新興市場貨幣組成的一籃子貨幣，自2024年底以來報酬約22%；以美元融資的利差交易已連續7季取得正報酬，是2008年以來最長紀錄。儘管土耳其里拉貶值26%，當地殖利率高於32%仍使土耳其債券維持獲利；哥倫比亞資產則兼具高收益與貨幣升值。

主要威脅是美國政策利率預期再度上升並推高美元。週五美債短端遭到拋售，顯示這項風險並未消失。不過，美元指數全週仍然下跌，許多拉丁美洲與東歐央行也持續提供偏高的實質利率。因此，利差交易仍有收益支撐，但若Warsh釋出聯準會將加快緊縮的訊號，相關報酬將更為脆弱。

## 恆大與Braskem加深困境債不確定性

中國大陸法院判處恆大創辦人許家印無期徒刑並下令沒收其資產，使恆大清算程序更加複雜。許家印旗下公司合計遭罰人民幣158億元，約合$24億。這項裁決使中國大陸的執法程序，可能與由香港主導、為債權人追索資產的行動發生衝突。

恆大清算人表示，這家開發商的債務約為$450億，並持續在全球追索許家印約$77億的資產。即使中國法律通常規定，賠償與償債順位優先於罰款及沒收，若中國大陸當局控制其中部分財產，境外債權人仍可能面臨額外的法律與實務障礙。

這套優先順位如何適用於涉及多個司法管轄區法院與資產的跨境清算，仍有不確定性。中國大陸的沒收命令能否在海外執行，也可能取決於當地法律。香港清算人對許家印提出的索賠尚未勝訴，因此判決與資產查扣的先後順序，將實質影響最終回收。

市場價格早已反映嚴重損失。裁決公布後，恆大多數境外債券仍低於每$1面額2美分。Deloitte在2023年估計，公司美元債在清算下的平均回收率可能為3.4%。最新判決並未確立更低的回收率，但使創辦人資產周圍多出另一個請求權人與執法程序。

清算人同時挑戰一項規模HK$10億、為恆大少數股東設立補償基金的安排。恆大重整多次失敗後，香港法院於2024年下令清算；這項爭議又為資產分配增添新的問題。債券持有人如今不再只是討論能否取回面額中的一小部分，而是必須面對有多少程序會競逐這筆有限回收。

Braskem則逼近更迫切的期限。這家巴西石化生產商表示，與債權人的協商已轉趨密集，公司也收到涉及新資本及資產擔保權益的非約束性提案，但重整條件尚未達成協議。法院下令提供的強制執行保護將於8月24日到期。

依巴西法律，Braskem若要進行庭外重整，必須取得合計持有至少三分之一債務的債權人支持。達到這項門檻後，各方可再獲得90天敲定條件。若無法達成協議或延長保護期，Braskem可能必須申請司法重整，相當於巴西的破產程序。

包括Elliott Investment Management與Contrarian Capital Management在內的債權人，已要求控股股東Petrobras提供財務支持，形式可能包括股本、營運資金或次順位債務。Petrobras也在考慮改善商業合約的付款條件。由於這家國營石油公司在選舉年與IG4 Capital共同控制Braskem，其參與使談判具有政治重要性。

財務壓力已擴散至整個集團。墨西哥子公司Braskem Idesa因流動性惡化，於本週在美國申請預先安排的破產保護。Braskem於2031年到期的美元債殖利率約為23%，價格已明確反映困境債風險。公司週五披露談判仍未解決後，股價一度下跌4.5%。

兩起事件反映不同的困境階段。恆大在多年違約與重整失敗後，債權人正爭奪有限且高度不確定的回收；Braskem則仍有短暫窗口，可在進入更廣泛法院程序的可能性升高前，協商新資本、擔保品及股東支持。兩案的回收結果都更取決於法律順位與資產控制權，而非整體信用市場走向。

## 後市意義

Bessent週一舉行記者會，將是財政部能否超越債務管理操作的最近考驗。投資人需要看到支出、收入或未來借款的量化變化，才能判斷這項財政方案是否足以改變公共債務突破$40兆的軌跡。進一步回購或減少長期公債發行，可以改變民間持有債務的期限結構；但若沒有財政節省，整體融資需求仍不會下降。

同時提出的伊朗方案另有通膨風險。市場將評估孤立德黑蘭的措施，是否實質限制石油出口、航運、保險或支付管道。儘管Pezeshkian呼籲結束戰爭，布蘭特原油週五仍收在$94.39，顯示單一和解言論並未使交易員相信供應中斷正在緩解。若措施獲得有效執行，即使財政方案起初支撐債券，能源通膨仍可能升高。

週三公布的7月個人消費支出物價數據，將檢驗週五實質殖利率上升、損益兩平通膨率下降的分化。經濟學家預期整體指數年增3.6%，為四個月來最小增幅，經通膨調整的消費者支出則變化不大。若細項溫和，將支持持續反通膨比回購更能長久壓低殖利率的看法；若價格壓力更廣泛或更強，則會強化7月聯準會辯論中支持緊縮的理由。

Warsh週五在Jackson Hole的演說，是更重要的政策反應函數事件。投資人將關注聯準會主席如何區分持續性通膨與能源效應、是否把長期殖利率上升視為有效的緊縮力量，以及財政部主動調整存續期間供給時，他會從市場價格擷取多少訊息。Warsh在7月會議後提供的指引有限，促成期限溢價上升，因此政策論述是否清楚，本身也會影響長端。

明尼亞波利斯聯準銀行總裁Neel Kashkari週日另行釋出政策訊號。Kashkari是7月支持升息25個基點的三名投票委員之一；他表示美國公債市場運作良好，殖利率上升不太可能影響聯準會決策。他仍不相信通膨會迅速回到目標，但拒絕預先判斷9月決定。這番說法保留緊縮傾向，卻不把債市賣壓視為需要干預或必然調整利率的理由。

韓國央行週四的決策，將檢驗出口強勁是否足以壓過觀察7月升息效果的理由。半導體與電腦出口動能顯著、核心通膨加速，第2季經濟成長也高於預期。若連續第二次升息，將確認官員認為科技榮景足以抵禦借款成本上升；若維持利率不變，市場焦點將轉向10月，但緊縮傾向不會因此消失。

日本財政日程啟動之際，最終融資全貌仍未出爐。創紀錄的預算申請與3.8%的暫定利率假設，將使債務服務成本受到關注；但補充預算支出的重新分類，使投資人無法單憑總額判斷財政擴張。最終預算與公債發行計畫必須顯示，¥370兆投資架構及初始預算擴大，究竟伴隨多少真正新增的借款。

AI債務融資管線仍是資本市場容量的實際考驗。由大型科技公司支持的交易仍可吸引大量需求，但殖利率高於7%之所以能吸引高收益債投資人，正是因為傳統買方要求更多補償。後續交易將顯示，跨界需求能否擴大到足以承接供給，或融資成本升高是否開始延後專案並限制較弱借款人。

Braskem的8月24日期限，是最近的困境債事件。若取得合計持有至少三分之一債務的債權人同意，公司便可取得90天時間推進庭外重整；若無法取得支持、擔保品或新資金，司法重整的可能性將升高，也能進一步看出Petrobras願意提供多少協助。

綜合這些事件，關鍵在於週五的熊市趨平，究竟會擴大為市場對聯準會政策的全面重新評估，還是僅為單一交易日對景氣活動轉強的反應。2年期殖利率已對成長數據作出反應，長端則維持在先前觸發財政部干預的水準附近。PCE、Bessent與Warsh將決定這些壓力會重新匯合，還是繼續使殖利率曲線分裂為近期貨幣政策風險與長期資金競爭兩端。

overall_summary.session_narrative:
美債殖利率全線上升，其中2年期殖利率上升4.7個基點至4.237%；強勁的企業活動數據顯示，聯準會忽略高於目標通膨的空間可能縮小。10年期殖利率上升2.9個基點至4.735%；其中實質殖利率上升4.8個基點至2.402%，損益兩平通膨率則下降1.9個基點至2.333%。這項結構顯示，行情主因是成長轉強與實質利率預期升高，而非能源再次帶動通膨重新定價。2年期與10年期利差收窄1.8個基點，扭轉前一交易日的部分陡峭化；不過，財政與存續期間壓力持續存在，30年期殖利率一個月來仍上升13.9個基點。

財政部擴大回購的計畫到收盤時已失去最初影響力，投資人轉而關注Scott Bessent即將提出的財政方案，究竟會降低借款需求，還是只重新分配存續期間。股票市場風險偏好仍具韌性；美元走弱，加上黃金與比特幣上漲，也維持市場對美元資產以外替代品的需求。信用融資依然暢通，但殖利率高於7%的AI專案日益需要高收益債投資人承接；恆大與Braskem則顯示，困境債結果取決於法律順位、擔保品與股東支持，而非整體市場方向。

## Opening Fixed-Income Thesis

Treasuries ended Aug. 21 lower as unexpectedly strong business activity shifted the pressure toward policy-sensitive maturities and reversed part of the curve steepening that had accompanied the week’s fiscal anxiety. The 2-year yield rose 4.7 basis points to 4.237%, the 5-year increased 3.4 basis points to 4.425%, the 10-year climbed 2.9 basis points to 4.735% and the 30-year added 2.3 basis points to 5.272%.

The session’s composition was more important than the modest scale of the selloff. S&P Global gauges showed US business activity expanding at its fastest pace in more than four years, supporting the possibility that the Federal Reserve may still need to raise rates despite softer employment, retail-sales and underlying inflation readings. The 10-year real yield rose 4.8 basis points to 2.402%, while the 10-year breakeven declined 1.9 basis points to 2.333%. Friday’s increase in nominal yields was therefore driven by real rates rather than another extension of the energy-related inflation repricing seen a day earlier.

The front end underperformed. The 2s10s curve flattened 1.8 basis points to 49.8 basis points, and 2s30s narrowed 2.4 basis points to 103.5 basis points. That was a change from the previous session, when inflation compensation and long-end fiscal pressure had produced a modest steepening. It did not reverse the much larger monthly move: the 30-year yield remained 13.9 basis points higher over one month, compared with a 2.7-basis-point decline in the 2-year, leaving the longer-run fiscal and duration premium intact.

Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent’s expanded buyback plan was no longer producing lower yields. The department’s midweek promise to at least double purchases of selected 10- to 30-year securities had generated a sharp but brief rally, after which the 10-year finished the week at 4.735% and the 30-year at 5.272%. Traders were left waiting for details of Bessent’s promised fiscal initiative and assessing whether Treasury would alter long-term issuance if yields rose again. President Donald Trump said Friday that Bessent had chosen to intervene on his own authority rather than at the president’s direction.

Cross-asset markets placed that bond weakness beside resilient risk appetite and continuing demand for alternatives to dollar assets. The S&P 500 gained 0.43% and the Nasdaq 100 rose 0.33%, although the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index fell 0.51% and finished the week down 5.45%. The Dollar Index slipped 0.10% on Friday and 0.87% over the week. Gold futures rose 2.39% to $4,624.10, taking their weekly gain to 5.56%, while Bitcoin traded around $77,000 after a short squeeze and renewed inflows produced its strongest weekly advance in more than three years.

Oil did not give the rates market a uniform inflation signal. WTI fell 0.88% to $87.06, but Brent rose 0.65% to $94.39 and ended the week 6.63% higher. Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian called for an end to the war, briefly pulling crude from its session highs, but other Iranian officials continued to favor fighting and prices recovered. The decline in the 10-year breakeven showed that Friday’s Treasury selloff was not simply another response to crude; stronger activity and higher real yields supplied the clearer explanation.

Credit remained available, but its distribution increasingly reflected the cost and volume of the artificial-intelligence investment cycle. Investment-grade data-center projects offering yields above 7% drew participation from high-yield investors, while Alphabet’s record Australian-dollar transaction exposed both the breadth and the limits of alternative funding markets. In distressed credit, Evergrande’s offshore creditors faced a more complicated recovery path after a mainland court ordered the confiscation of founder Hui Ka Yan’s assets, and Braskem approached the expiration of its creditor shield without an agreed restructuring.

## Stronger Activity Tests the Limits of Treasury’s Intervention

Friday’s Treasury move extended the rapid loss of confidence in the durability of the buyback rally. Two days earlier, the announcement of larger long-duration repurchases had driven yields sharply lower by offering an official source of demand for older 10- to 30-year securities. By the end of the week, investors had restored most of that yield premium as growth, inflation, deficits and competing corporate issuance continued to determine the market-clearing level.

The stronger S&P Global activity readings brought the Fed back into that calculation. The 2-year yield’s 4.7-basis-point increase exceeded the rise at every longer benchmark, while the real-yield increase exceeded the change in the nominal 10-year because breakeven inflation fell. The result was not a renewed inflation scare. It was a judgment that an economy maintaining strong business momentum may give policymakers less room to look through above-target inflation, even if recent employment and retail data have been weaker.

Interest-rate swaps on Friday implied about a 40% probability of a September rate increase, with a full move priced only around year-end. Those expectations remain sensitive to incoming inflation evidence because the July Federal Open Market Committee meeting produced three dissents in favor of a hike and several nonvoting officials subsequently expressed support for tighter policy. At the same time, benign underlying inflation and disappointing labor and spending data have prevented that tightening coalition from becoming a settled market expectation.

The buyback initiative operates on a different part of the yield curve. Bessent described the department’s approach as a “Treasury twist”: buying longer maturities while relying more heavily on shorter debt for financing. Such a maturity switch can reduce the duration private investors must hold, but it does not lower total borrowing and makes the government’s funding cost more sensitive to future short-term rates. With federal debt above $40 trillion and annual interest expense running above $1 trillion, investors are still looking for evidence that debt management will be paired with a narrower deficit.

Bessent said he and White House budget director Russ Vought would examine both revenue and spending, including fraud reduction and lower transfers to states. No quantified fiscal effect had been provided by Friday’s close. Social Security, Medicare and Medicaid are major drivers of a deficit forecast near 6% of gross domestic product, and Evercore ISI strategist Sarah Bianchi judged material near-term savings unlikely without changes to politically protected programs.

Treasury could also adjust the composition of future auctions. A recent change in its issuance guidance encouraged speculation that officials might restrain sales of the longest maturities and concentrate additional borrowing in bills and intermediate tenors. Bessent separately urged AI companies to consider issuing more 5-year debt rather than adding to the long end. Those steps could affect where supply reaches investors, but they would leave the government and corporate sectors competing for the same aggregate pool of capital.

The uncertainty is already raising questions about the predictability of debt management. Treasury said the buybacks were intended to improve liquidity in older securities, yet JPMorgan’s rates strategists found that market functioning had improved notably this year. Investors may therefore interpret any further intervention as a response to the level of yields rather than a routine liquidity operation. Western Asset portfolio manager Robert Abad said additional purchases or changes to long-end issuance would provide stronger evidence that officials were reacting to borrowing costs themselves.

Friday’s trading occurred with less activity than the prior session. FINRA recorded $979.7 billion of Treasury par volume, down 21.4%, including $832.4 billion of nominal coupons, down 18.1%. Activity in maturities beyond 20 years fell 35.8% to $88.5 billion. The figures do not reveal whether customers bought or sold, but they show that yields rose while turnover was receding from the heavier adjustment that followed the initial intervention.

The market also shifted the pressure outside Treasuries. Gold’s advance, the weaker dollar and Bitcoin’s surge reflected concern that attempts to contain long-term yields could transfer part of the adjustment into the currency or scarce assets. Bitcoin climbed as much as 9.4% on Friday, with about $2.5 billion of bearish Bitcoin positions and $4.5 billion across cryptocurrencies liquidated over three days. US-listed spot Bitcoin funds attracted more than $1 billion during the week.

Forced covering accounted for a substantial part of the cryptocurrency move, limiting its value as a clean fiscal signal. Gold rose without the same liquidation mechanism, however, and finished the month to date about 13.58% higher. The Dollar Index’s decline to 98.8 left it 2.35% lower over one month. Treasury’s intervention had therefore failed to secure a lasting bond rally while the assets most closely associated with currency and fiscal hedging retained their gains.

The equity response was less defensive. The S&P 500 and Nasdaq 100 rose as the strong activity data supported the earnings outlook, and the VIX fell 5.50% to 15.13. Still, the S&P 500 lost 1.43% over the week and the Nasdaq 100 fell 2.45%, while semiconductor shares suffered a much larger weekly decline. Higher real yields and the funding burden attached to the AI buildout continued to raise the hurdle for long-duration equity valuations even when aggregate indexes advanced.

The market’s message was therefore divided by horizon. Strong activity lifted near-term real-rate expectations and flattened the curve on Friday. Over the month, heavy government borrowing, persistent inflation uncertainty and private demand for capital kept the long end under greater pressure. Larger buybacks can alter that distribution temporarily, but Friday’s close showed that they had not displaced the economic and fiscal forces setting yields.

## AI Financing Pulls High-Yield Buyers Into Investment-Grade Debt

The AI capital cycle is increasingly blurring the conventional boundary between investment-grade and high-yield demand. QTS Realty Trust sold $3.9 billion of bonds to finance a Microsoft-linked data-center project in Georgia at a yield of about 7.23%. The securities carried high-grade ratings, but underwriters placed them with both investment-grade and junk-bond investors because the yield exceeded what many middle-tier speculative-grade borrowers ordinarily offer.

BlackRock paid an even higher 7.53% yield in July on investment-grade securities financing a Texas data-center project. In secondary trading, obligations from issuers including Oracle and SpaceX were also changing hands at yields associated with junk debt. The crossover demand shows that buyers are distinguishing between formal ratings and the compensation required for construction risk, lease concentration, repeated issuance and uncertain project payoffs.

Companies have borrowed more than $410 billion for data centers and other AI investment during 2026. Vanguard estimates hyperscalers could spend almost $800 billion this year and more than $1 trillion annually from 2027 through 2030, with most of that expenditure financed in debt markets. That prospective supply helps explain why even highly rated projects must offer yields capable of attracting investors beyond the traditional investment-grade buyer base.

The additional demand is useful but finite. The US high-yield market is about $1.5 trillion, less than one-fifth the size of its investment-grade counterpart, and its investors would need to sell existing holdings to fund a large rotation into high-grade technology debt. The crossover bid therefore broadens distribution for individual transactions without supplying unlimited capacity for the financing pipeline.

Higher yields may eventually regulate the volume. Large technology companies with strong balance sheets can absorb expensive funding while waiting years for data-center investments to produce cash flow. Smaller borrowers have less room to do so. Morgan Stanley strategists expect wider spreads to constrain lower-rated issuers first, making funding costs a brake on future supply even if the largest hyperscalers continue spending.

Alphabet’s Australian-dollar transaction provided a different test of market capacity. The company raised A$5.5 billion in its first Australian bond sale, the largest corporate offering in the country, after receiving more than A$18 billion of orders. The deal formed part of more than $80 billion of debt Alphabet has issued this year across US, Canadian and Australian dollars, euros, Swiss francs, sterling and yen.

The Australian market offered currency diversification and a deep pension-fund buyer base, while cross-currency swaps allowed Alphabet to convert proceeds into the funding it required. Its 20-year Australian bond priced broadly in line with its US borrowing cost after swapping back into dollars. For local investors, the transaction supplied a large international issuer at yields above those available from similarly rated domestic banks.

The allocation also revealed the market’s limits. Queensland Investment Corporation bid for A$300 million across the tranches and received about A$170 million. Marayka Ward, the manager’s director of fixed-income strategy, expects more Big Tech issuance but judged that Australia may have room for only a couple of transactions of that scale each year. She also said another hyperscaler might not receive the same reception as Alphabet, particularly if investors viewed its business as less defensive.

Foreign borrowers have sold more than A$64 billion of Australian-dollar bonds this year, putting the market on course for another record. Yet that total remains small beside roughly $1.5 trillion of US high-grade issuance. Australia can diversify funding for selected issuers; it cannot absorb the broader hyperscaler pipeline at US scale.

The expansion is changing hedging activity as well. Open interest in the front-month 3-year Australian government-bond futures contract reached 1.4 million contracts on Thursday, the highest since May 2019 and close to the 1.43 million record set in 2008. The market value of Australian-dollar bonds has risen almost 40% from its October 2022 low to A$2.14 trillion, increasing demand from dealers and investors to hedge interest-rate exposure.

These developments give the AI financing boom a direct connection to sovereign curves without requiring a deterioration in corporate credit quality. Large project and corporate transactions add duration, consume dealer balance sheet and compete with governments for investors. High-grade ratings preserve access, but transactions yielding above 7% show that access is clearing at a price consistent with the scale and uncertainty of the buildout.

## Global Policy Signals Diverge as Inflation and Growth Separate

Europe supplied a more favorable set of wage and expectations data without resolving the case for another European Central Bank increase. Negotiated pay rose 2.44% from a year earlier in Q2, down from a revised 2.56% in the previous quarter and far below the 5.55% peak reached in 2024. The moderation reduced evidence that the energy shock was feeding quickly into wages, although the ECB’s tracker anticipates some acceleration through early 2027.

Consumer inflation expectations also edged lower. Households surveyed by the ECB expected prices to rise 2.9% over the following year in July, down from 3% in June. The 3-year measure declined to 2.7% from 2.8%. Expectations remained above the ECB’s 2% target, but the direction was reassuring after the Iran conflict drove substantial volatility in oil and gas markets.

Governing Council member Martins Kazaks kept the policy choice open. He described inflation near 3% as somewhat uncomfortable and said the ECB was positioned to act if needed, while emphasizing that the September decision would depend on updated data and projections. He also cited stronger-than-expected Q2 growth and low unemployment, but acknowledged slowing wages and anchored expectations.

That combination leaves the ECB weighing current inflation against evidence that second-round effects remain contained. Markets were close to pricing another 25-basis-point increase after June’s initial hike. The wage and expectations figures make immediate tightening less automatic, but they do not remove the risk that energy costs persist or spread into services and corporate pricing.

Switzerland remains at the opposite end of the inflation problem. Swiss National Bank policymaker Petra Tschudin said the central bank would take rates below zero if necessary to keep inflation within its 0% to 2% range. The SNB cut its benchmark to zero last year and has held it there, while inflation slowed to 0.4% in July despite higher global energy prices. Stronger-than-expected Q2 growth and rising wages provide counterevidence, but Tschudin’s statement preserved negative rates as an available tool rather than treating zero as a floor.

South Korea’s trade data strengthened the case for further tightening. Working-day-adjusted exports rose 61.5% from a year earlier in the first 20 days of August, after an initially reported 62.9% increase over the comparable July period. Unadjusted shipments gained 56%, imports rose 19% and the trade surplus approached $14 billion.

Semiconductors led the expansion with a 198.8% increase, while computer-related exports rose 242.1%. Shipments to China gained 118.6% and those to the US increased 59.4%. Automobile exports fell about 45%, showing that the strength remained concentrated in technology rather than uniformly distributed across industries.

The Bank of Korea raised its policy rate by 25 basis points to 2.75% in July and maintained a tightening bias. Headline inflation subsequently slowed to 2.8%, but core inflation accelerated to 2.6%, while Q2 growth reached a stronger-than-expected 0.6%. The export windfall gives the economy more capacity to withstand another increase, leaving the next meeting divided between a back-to-back move and waiting until October.

Japan faces a different combination of monetary normalization and fiscal supply. Budget requests for the fiscal year beginning in April are expected to exceed the previous record of ¥122 trillion. The Finance Ministry is considering a provisional interest rate of 3.8% for calculating next year’s debt-service costs, up from 2.6% in the current fiscal plan. With interest expense already consuming about one-quarter of the budget, the higher assumption would make rising JGB yields visible in official spending estimates.

The headline request total may overstate the underlying fiscal expansion. Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi wants to move recurring programs from supplementary budgets into the initial plan, and some of last year’s ¥18.3 trillion extra budget may therefore appear earlier in the process. Ministries can also seek uncapped funding for capital investment tied to a ¥370 trillion, 14-year growth strategy through a separate multi-year framework financed partly with bridge bonds.

Those changes make historical comparisons difficult but do not eliminate the funding burden. Ministries are expected to begin submitting requests in the coming week, while the final budget and bond-issuance plan will not be clear until around year-end. Investors must distinguish greater transparency about existing spending from genuinely larger commitments, particularly as higher assumed interest rates raise the cost of both refinancing and new issuance.

China’s weekend growth assessments added a softer demand signal to the global picture. Goldman Sachs estimated that annualized economic expansion had slowed to about 4% early in Q3 from 4.3% in the prior quarter, below Beijing’s 4.5% to 5% annual target. BNP Paribas estimated 4.1%, while Macquarie put the pace at about 4.2%. Weak July industrial production, consumption and investment led Goldman to characterize the slowdown as demand-driven.

Expectations for monetary easing consequently increased, although the policy path is constrained by higher oil prices and factory-gate inflation. Economists surveyed in July generally expected the People’s Bank of China to leave its policy rate unchanged this year and next, while regarding a Q4 reduction in banks’ reserve requirement ratio as more likely. Officials have so far favored loan subsidies and other targeted financing support over broad rate reductions.

The global divergence remains supportive of selected emerging-market carry trades. A basket of 8 major EM currencies has returned about 22% since the end of 2024, and dollar-funded carry has produced positive returns for 7 consecutive quarters, the longest run since 2008. Local yields above 32% have kept Turkish bonds profitable despite a 26% decline in the lira, while Colombian assets combined high income with currency appreciation.

The principal threat is a renewed rise in expected US policy rates that strengthens the dollar. Friday’s front-end Treasury selloff showed that risk had not disappeared. The Dollar Index nevertheless finished the week lower, and many Latin American and eastern European central banks continue to offer high real rates. That leaves carry supported by income but increasingly vulnerable to any Warsh signal that shifts the Fed toward faster tightening.

## Evergrande and Braskem Deepen Distressed-Credit Uncertainty

Evergrande’s liquidation became more complicated after a mainland court sentenced founder Hui Ka Yan to life in prison and ordered his assets confiscated. His companies were fined a combined 15.8 billion yuan, or about $2.4 billion. The ruling introduced a potential conflict between mainland enforcement and the Hong Kong-led effort to recover assets for creditors.

Evergrande’s liquidators have said the developer carried about $45 billion of debt and have been pursuing approximately $7.7 billion of Hui’s assets worldwide. If mainland authorities take control of part of that property, offshore creditors may face additional legal and practical barriers even though Chinese law generally gives compensation and debt repayment priority over fines and confiscation.

The application of that priority is uncertain in a cross-border liquidation involving courts and assets in multiple jurisdictions. Overseas enforcement of a mainland confiscation order may also depend on local law. Hong Kong liquidators have not yet prevailed in their claim against Hui, leaving the sequence of judgments and asset seizures material to the eventual recovery.

Market pricing already assumes a severe loss. Most Evergrande offshore bonds remained below 2 cents on the dollar after the ruling. Deloitte estimated in 2023 that the company’s dollar-note recovery in liquidation could average 3.4%. The latest judgment does not establish a lower recovery, but it creates another claimant and enforcement process around the founder’s assets.

The liquidators are simultaneously challenging a HK$1 billion arrangement that created a compensation fund for Evergrande minority shareholders. The dispute adds another potential allocation question to a liquidation that began after failed restructuring attempts and a Hong Kong court order in 2024. Bondholders are no longer debating whether they will recover only a small fraction of face value; they are confronting how many proceedings may compete for that fraction.

Braskem approached a more immediate deadline. The Brazilian petrochemical producer said creditor discussions had intensified and that it had received nonbinding proposals involving new capital and security interests over assets, but no restructuring terms had been agreed. Its court-ordered protection from enforcement was due to expire Aug. 24.

The company needs support from holders of at least one-third of its debt to pursue an out-of-court restructuring under Brazilian law. Reaching that threshold would give the parties another 90 days to finalize terms. Without an agreement or extended protection, Braskem may need to seek judicial recovery, Brazil’s equivalent of bankruptcy proceedings.

Creditors including Elliott Investment Management and Contrarian Capital Management have pressed controlling shareholder Petrobras for financial support, potentially through equity, working capital or junior debt. Petrobras has also been considering improved payment terms on commercial contracts. Its involvement gives the negotiation political importance because the state-controlled oil company shares control of Braskem with IG4 Capital in an election year.

Financial stress has already spread across the group. Mexican subsidiary Braskem Idesa filed for prepackaged US bankruptcy protection during the week as liquidity deteriorated. Braskem’s dollar bonds due in 2031 yielded about 23%, pricing the debt firmly in distressed territory. The company’s shares fell as much as 4.5% Friday after it disclosed that negotiations remained unresolved.

The two cases illustrate different stages of distress. Evergrande creditors are competing over a small and uncertain recovery after years of default and failed restructuring. Braskem still has a short window to negotiate capital, collateral and shareholder support before a broader court process becomes more likely. In both, legal priority and asset control matter more than the broad direction of credit markets.

## Forward Market Significance

Bessent’s Monday press conference is the nearest test of whether Treasury can move beyond debt-management tactics. Investors need quantified changes to spending, revenue or future borrowing to judge whether the fiscal initiative alters the trajectory that pushed public debt above $40 trillion. Further buybacks or lower long-term issuance would change the maturity of debt in private hands, but without fiscal savings they would leave the total financing requirement intact.

The accompanying Iran plan carries a separate inflation risk. Markets will assess whether efforts to isolate Tehran materially restrict oil exports, shipping, insurance or payment channels. Brent ended Friday at $94.39 despite Pezeshkian’s call to end the war, showing that one conciliatory statement had not persuaded traders that supply disruption was easing. Effective enforcement could lift energy inflation even if the fiscal announcement initially supports bonds.

July personal-consumption-expenditure inflation on Wednesday will test the split between Friday’s higher real yields and lower breakevens. Economists expect the headline index to rise 3.6% from a year earlier, the smallest annual increase in four months, with little change in inflation-adjusted consumer spending. A benign composition would support the argument that sustained disinflation offers a more durable route to lower yields than buybacks. Broader or firmer pressure would strengthen the tightening case documented in the July Fed debate.

Warsh’s Jackson Hole address on Friday is the larger reaction-function event. Investors will look for how the Fed chair separates persistent inflation from energy effects, whether he regards higher long yields as useful restraint and how much information he takes from market prices when Treasury is actively changing duration supply. His limited guidance after the July meeting contributed to the rise in term premium, making clarity itself relevant to the long end.

Minneapolis Fed President Neel Kashkari added a distinct policy signal on Sunday. Kashkari, one of the three July voters who favored a 25-basis-point increase, said the Treasury market was functioning well and that higher yields were unlikely to affect the Fed’s deliberations. He remained unconvinced that inflation was returning to target quickly, but declined to prejudge September. His comments preserve a tightening bias without treating the bond selloff as a reason for either intervention or an automatic rate response.

The Bank of Korea’s Thursday decision will test whether export strength outweighs the case for observing the effects of July’s increase. Semiconductor and computer shipments show substantial momentum, core inflation has accelerated and the economy grew faster than expected in Q2. A second consecutive hike would confirm that officials view the technology boom as sufficient protection against tighter borrowing costs; a hold would shift attention to October without removing the tightening bias.

Japan’s fiscal calendar begins before its final financing picture is available. Record budget requests and a provisional 3.8% interest assumption will draw attention to debt-service costs, but the reclassification of supplementary spending prevents a clean reading from the headline total alone. The eventual budget and bond-issuance plan must show how much genuinely new borrowing accompanies the ¥370 trillion investment framework and the shift toward a larger initial budget.

The AI debt pipeline remains a practical test of capital-market capacity. Transactions backed by large technology companies can still draw heavy demand, but yields above 7% are attracting high-yield investors precisely because conventional buyers require greater compensation. Further deals will show whether crossover demand broadens enough to absorb supply or whether higher funding costs begin delaying projects and constraining weaker borrowers.

Braskem’s Aug. 24 deadline is the nearest distressed-credit event. Agreement from at least one-third of creditors would open a 90-day route toward an out-of-court restructuring. Failure to secure support, collateral or new money would increase the likelihood of judicial recovery and clarify how much assistance Petrobras is prepared to provide.

Across these events, the decisive question is whether Friday’s bear flattening develops into a broader reassessment of Fed policy or remains a one-session response to stronger activity. The 2-year yield reacted to growth while the long end stayed anchored near the levels that had already triggered Treasury intervention. PCE, Bessent and Warsh will determine whether those pressures converge again or continue to divide the curve between near-term monetary policy and longer-term competition for capital.

overall_summary.headline: Strong US activity drives a real-yield-led Treasury selloff as buyback relief fades
overall_summary.session_narrative:
Treasury yields rose across the curve, led by a 4.7-basis-point increase in the 2-year yield to 4.237%, after strong business-activity data suggested that the Fed may have less room to look through above-target inflation. The 10-year yield climbed 2.9 basis points to 4.735%, with its real yield up 4.8 basis points to 2.402% while the breakeven fell 1.9 basis points to 2.333%. That composition pointed to stronger growth and higher real-rate expectations rather than another energy-led inflation repricing. The 2s10s curve flattened 1.8 basis points, reversing part of the prior session’s steepening, although the 30-year yield remained 13.9 basis points higher over one month as fiscal and duration pressure persisted.

Treasury’s expanded buyback plan had lost its initial influence by the close, leaving investors focused on whether Scott Bessent’s coming fiscal initiative will reduce borrowing needs or merely redistribute duration. Risk appetite nevertheless held up in equities, while a weaker dollar and gains in gold and Bitcoin preserved demand for alternatives to dollar assets. Credit remained available, but AI projects yielding above 7% increasingly required high-yield buyers, while Evergrande and Braskem showed that legal priority, collateral and shareholder support—not broad market direction—were driving distressed outcomes.
overall_summary.summary: Treasuries fell as the fastest US business expansion in more than four years revived tightening risk, lifting real yields and the policy-sensitive front end even as larger long-duration buybacks failed to produce lasting relief.
